subject: Chemistry
topic: Structure and polarity of the carbonyl group
title: The Carbonyl Group: Structure and Polarity
summary: Why the carbon of C=O is every nucleophile's target: an sp², planar carbon, a π bond from sideways p–p overlap, and a polar C=O with δ⁺ carbon and δ⁻ oxygen, explained by resonance.

notes.title: 02 – Structure and Polarity of the Carbonyl Group

keyPoints: The carbonyl carbon is **sp²**: three σ bonds in **one plane**, about **120°** apart (trigonal planar).
The **π bond** comes from sideways overlap of C and O **p orbitals**; the π cloud lies **above and below** the plane.
O is more electronegative: **O δ⁻ (nucleophilic)**, **C δ⁺ (electrophilic)**; carbonyl compounds are **more polar than ethers**.
Resonance **C=O ⟷ C⁺–O⁻**: the real molecule is a hybrid, so **nucleophiles attack the carbon**.

head: Feature
Carbonyl group
rows: sideways overlap of C and O p orbitals; cloud above and below the plane

blocks.p: Oxygen pulls the bonding electrons, so **carbon is δ⁺** (electrophilic, a Lewis acid) and **oxygen is δ⁻** (nucleophilic, a Lewis base). Resonance between **R₂C=O** and **R₂C⁺–O⁻** explains the large dipole moment; the real molecule is a hybrid, and a nucleophile attacks the carbon.
